The local networking group, Ladies Out Lunching – LOL for short – will host their July Luncheon at Lost Pizza Company in Benton, Wednesday, August 19th from 12:00 – 1:00 pm. 

Come ready to chat and make some new friends! 

Luncheon Details:

– Lunch is Dutch Treat: just order and pay your meal.

– Don’t forget to bring your business cards and materials!

– Happy Gift: If you would like a minute to share about your business bring a small gift or some business swag to share! We will draw for a recipient and you get a chance to share – everyone loves a present… right?

NONPROFIT SUPPORT! This month we are collecting nonperishable food items and feminine hygiene products for local food pantries.

LOL meets the 3rd Wednesday of each month at various restaurants around Saline County.  Learn more about LOL and RSVP to an event by visiting  www.facebook.com/groups/ladiesoutlunching/

item.title: Entergy suspends disconnects through August 21 amid extreme heat wave
item.dc:creator: Shelli Poole
item.description: Entergy Arkansas has announced a temporary suspension of residential service disconnections for all customers through Friday, August 21, to protect public safety during a period of extreme heat. The utility provider confirmed that disconnection procedures will not resume until Monday, August 24, as dangerous temperatures continue to impact communities across the state. Read more below. […]
item.content:encoded:
Entergy Arkansas has announced a temporary suspension of residential service disconnections for all customers through Friday, August 21, to protect public safety during a period of extreme heat. The utility provider confirmed that disconnection procedures will not resume until Monday, August 24, as dangerous temperatures continue to impact communities across the state. Read more below.




The temporary suspension is a proactive safety measure intended to help residents keep their cooling systems running during the ongoing heat wave. Company officials noted that while they are pausing disconnections, this does not prevent the possibility of unexpected power outages caused by severe weather, emergencies, or equipment damage.

In addition to suspending shutoffs, Entergy Arkansas has issued a set of critical guidelines to help customers manage their energy usage and avoid heat-related health emergencies. Cooling costs typically represent the largest portion of a household’s electric bill during the summer, but several low-cost or no-cost strategies can significantly reduce energy consumption:

  • Adjust the thermostat:
    Residents are advised to set their thermostats to the highest temperature that remains comfortable.
  • Maintain air-conditioning units:
    Routinely cleaning or replacing air filters helps systems run more efficiently.
  • Utilize fans:
    Ceiling and portable fans can effectively circulate cool air, though they should be turned off when rooms are unoccupied.
  • Block sunlight:
    Closing blinds, curtains, and shades during the hottest afternoon hours helps keep indoor temperatures down.
  • Seal air leaks:
    Gaps around doors, windows, and ductwork should be sealed to keep conditioned air from escaping.

Entergy Arkansas offers energy-monitoring resources through its online portal, where customers can use myAdvisor tools to track real-time energy use and identify custom savings options. Additional energy-efficiency programs, rebates, and bill-assistance tools are available through the company’s online Bill Toolkit.

For those working outdoors, safety remains paramount. Health experts advise drinking plenty of water, scheduling strenuous labor during the coolest times of the day, and taking frequent breaks in shaded or air-conditioned areas. Signs of heat exhaustion include heavy sweating, headache, nausea, and extreme fatigue. If an individual shows signs of heat stroke—such as confusion, seizures, hot and dry skin, or loss of consciousness—emergency services should be contacted immediately.

For additional energy-saving, bill-management and customer assistance resources, visit Entergy Arkansas.

item.title: Saline County Flea Market and Trade Day is set for Aug 15th at Fairgrounds
item.dc:creator: Shelli Poole
item.description: The Saline County Fair Association is hosting its fourth Flea Market and Trade Day on Saturday, August 15, offering a diverse array of local merchandise, crafts, and food. Proceeds from this free event will directly fund ongoing efforts to rebuild and improve the Saline County Fairgrounds. Read more below. The community fundraiser, themed “Rebuilding Together,” […]
item.content:encoded:
The Saline County Fair Association is hosting its fourth Flea Market and Trade Day on Saturday, August 15, offering a diverse array of local merchandise, crafts, and food.

Proceeds from this free event will directly fund ongoing efforts to rebuild and improve the Saline County Fairgrounds. Read more below.




The community fundraiser, themed “Rebuilding Together,” is 7:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. at the Fairgrounds, at 406 Fairfield in Benton. The event will take place rain or shine, because the indoor vendor buildings are fully air-conditioned.

Shoppers can expect to find a wide variety of goods, including:

  • yard sale items,
  • flea market finds,
  • crafts,
  • antiques,
  • fresh produce,
  • eggs,
  • animals, and
  • animal supplies.

Come hungry,  because the Homemakers Extension kitchen and concession stand will be open, serving a variety of foods and treats to raise additional funds for the rebuilding project.

If you’d like to be a vendor, indoor and outdoor vendor spaces are still available. A 12×12-foot outside space costs $25, while a 10×10-foot inside space is $50. The spaces do not include tents, tables, chairs, electricity, or water, and all booth rental proceeds go directly toward the fairgrounds.

Vendor setup is scheduled for Friday evening from 4:30-7:00 p.m., and Saturday morning at 6:00 a.m. Participating businesses are required to meet all standard licensing requirements, and animal vendors must comply with applicable regulations.

Upcoming Flea Market and Trade Days are scheduled for September 26, October 24, and a two-day event on November 6 and 7. Interested vendors or attendees can request  information by texting 501-860-3101, emailing salinecofair@hotmail.com, or visiting the association’s online registration form.

item.title: Join History Society Aug 13th to celebrate 40 years
item.dc:creator: Shelli Poole
item.description: Join Saline County History & Heritage Society (SCHHS) for the 40th anniversary celebration on August 13th. Read more below. Come to commemorate the inception of the SCHHS back in 1986 as a nonprofit – preserving, researching, and exploring the history and heritage of our Saline County community. The fun is on Thursday, August 13. […]
item.content:encoded:
Join Saline County History & Heritage Society (SCHHS) for the 40th anniversary celebration on August 13th. Read more below.




Come to commemorate the inception of the SCHHS back in 1986 as a nonprofit – preserving, researching, and exploring the history and heritage of our Saline County community.

The fun is on Thursday, August 13. The program begins at 5:00 p.m. at 123 North Market St.

Show your support for history by attending this presentation, and bring a friend. There’s no charge to attend, and guests are welcome.

However, if you’d like to become a supporting member of the SCHHS, it’s $25 per year per household which helps to sustain our non-profit in educating the community on the county’s history, preservation of our great heritage, and providing a space for research.

Browse MySaline’s list of all the events in Saline County at www.mysaline.com/events.

item.title: Free beginner beekeeping workshop Tuesday at the Fairgrounds
item.dc:creator: Shelli Poole
item.description: Residents interested in learning the art of apiculture are invited to attend a free introductory beekeeping workshop at the Saline County Fairgrounds this August. item.content:encoded:
Residents interested in learning the art of apiculture are invited to attend a free introductory beekeeping workshop at the Saline County Fairgrounds this August.

The event will offer beginners a comprehensive overview of the practice, led by local experts from Southern Yankee Homestead. Read more below.




The workshop is scheduled to take place on Tuesday, August 18th, beginning at 6 p.m. at the Saline County Fairgrounds.

Hosted by Southern Yankee Homestead, this educational session is tailored specifically for beginners with little to no prior experience. Instructors will guide attendees through the fundamental basics of beekeeping, providing the foundational knowledge needed to safely start and maintain a healthy bee colony.

Admission to the workshop is completely FREE and open to the public. Anyone interested in attending or seeking more information about the event is encouraged to call or text the organizers at 501-860-3773.
